proofs.proof_tex:
We prove the assertions in four steps.

First fix a topological order of \(W\).  By \(\text{def:architecture-list}\), its saturated superarchitecture contains every forward directed argument and every formal source \(U_C\), \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq W\).  Consider any architecture having this order.  Replace each missing directed argument by a table argument on which the corresponding structural function is constant.  If a source is absent, put its mass vector at a simplex vertex, with one slot of mass one and all other slots of mass zero, and choose every incident table to be constant in that source argument.  Thus no all-zero vector is used.  If a source has actual child set \(D\), install its law and its table arguments in the formal slot \(U_D\).  When several sources have the same actual child set, first merge them as in the next paragraph.  These extensions change no structural equation on any effective argument and therefore change no factual or interventional solution.  Hence every formerly enumerated architecture embeds in one saturated architecture having the same order.  There are at most \(N!\) orders, so
\[
 A_{\max}=N!.
\]

We now justify the merging step and the active-child-set convention.  Group mutually independent exogenous sources according to their nonempty sets of retained children.  For each \(\varnothing\ne C\subseteq W\), let \(U_C\) be the tuple of all original sources having retained child set \(C\), with the product law inherited from those sources.  Tuples for distinct \(C\)'s use disjoint original coordinates and hence remain mutually independent.  Substitute the tuple coordinates into the old structural equations.  Evaluation in topological order shows, node by node, that every structural solution under every intervention is unchanged.  Moreover, a retained equation depends essentially on the tuple precisely when it depends essentially on at least one tuple coordinate.  One direction is immediate.  For the other, join two tuple values by changing one coordinate at a time; if the endpoint outputs differ, the output changes at some step.  Thus merging preserves the minimal structural graph.  Empty-child sources can be discarded.  There are \(2^N-1=H_{\max}\) nonempty subsets of \(W\).

The same argument verifies the normalization required by \(\text{def:graph-legality-stratum}\).  For a formal source \(U_C\), put
\[
 D_C=\{j\in C:Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}(T,p_T)>0\}.
\]
If \(D_C=\varnothing\), replace the source by the simplex-vertex source just described and make every incident table ignore it; this changes no solution outside an exogenous null set.  If \(D_C\ne\varnothing\), the essential-feature lemma says that its actual retained children are exactly \(D_C\).  Formal sources with the same \(D_C\) may then be merged into one tuple source.  Thus projection is applied only after empty realized child sets are discarded and duplicate realized child sets are merged.  This proves that the saturated labels do not create spurious actual sources.

Second, fix any permitted architecture with independent sources \(U_1,\ldots,U_H\), where \(H\le H_{\max}\).  Define
\[
 F(U_1,\ldots,U_H)=
 \left(
   (\mathbf 1\{V=v,S=1\})_{v\in\Omega_V},
   h(A^b)\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\},
   \mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}
 \right)\in\mathbb R^{m+2}.
\]
The boundedness of \(h\) and finiteness of \(\Omega_V\) make \(F\) integrable, and \(\mathbb E_M F=\zeta(M)\) by \(\text{def:moment-map}\).  Hold all source laws except that of \(U_k\) fixed and define
\[
 g_k(u)=
 \int F(u_1,\ldots,u_{k-1},u,u_{k+1},\ldots,u_H)
       \prod_{r\ne k}dP_r(u_r).
\]
Mutual independence and iterated integration give
\[
 \zeta(M)=\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]

We record the elementary barycenter argument used here.  If an integrable random vector \(Y\) takes values in \(\mathbb R^d\), then \(\mathbb EY\) belongs to the convex hull of its essential range.  Indeed, after translating by \(\mathbb EY\), suppose that zero is outside that convex hull.  Finite-dimensional separation supplies a nonzero linear functional nonnegative on the range.  Its expectation is zero, so it vanishes almost surely.  Restricting to its kernel lowers the affine dimension; induction gives the claimed convex-hull membership.  By the definition of convex hull there is a finite convex representation, and whenever it has more than \(d+1\) points an affine dependence permits changing the weights until one becomes zero while preserving their sum and barycenter.  Iteration leaves at most \(d+1\) actual essential-range values.

Apply this argument with \(d=m+2\).  There are \(L_k\le m+3=K_{\max}\), values \(u_{k,1},\ldots,u_{k,L_k}\), and weights \(w_{k,r}\ge0\) such that
\[
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}=1,\qquad
 \sum_{r=1}^{L_k}w_{k,r}g_k(u_{k,r})
 =\int g_k(u)\,dP_k(u).
\]
Replacing only \(P_k\) by this discrete law preserves \(\zeta(M)\) and product factorization.  Repeat for \(k=1,\ldots,H\), always using the currently installed laws of the other sources.  Every replacement preserves the whole moment vector, so the terminal model still has moment vector \(\zeta(M)\) and every source has at most \(K_{\max}\) values.  In particular,
\[
 \rho=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}c_v(M)
\]
is preserved as one common normalization.  Since retained state spaces and reduced source supports are finite, every structural function is a deterministic response table.  Embedding the reduced architecture in the saturated order only adds inessential directed inputs and simplex-vertex ignored sources, so its dense tables are among those counted by \(R_{\max}\).  This reduction does not assert that a strict inequality \(Z_e>0\) survives.

Third, take \((p_T,\rho)\in\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  Its saturated topological order, deterministic tables, and mutually independent source simplexes define a recursive finite SCM \(M_{T,p_T}\).  The graph-legality stratum first determines active incidence signs, discards empty realized source child sets, and merges duplicates.  The established essential-feature lemma then gives a \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) such that
\[
 G_S(M_{T,p_T})=G.
\]
The remaining constraints in \(\text{def:finite-legal-fiber}\) give, for each \(v\in\Omega_V\),
\[
 c_v(M_{T,p_T})=\Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v),\qquad
 \delta\le\rho\le1,\qquad
 d_{M_{T,p_T}}=\Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta.
\]
Together with \(\text{ass:positive-selected-law}\), these are exactly the conditions in \(\text{def:admissible-class}\).  Hence \(M_{T,p_T}\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\).  Since \(\delta>0\), the denominator is positive and
\[
 \theta(M_{T,p_T})
 =\frac{\Phi_T(p_T)_n}{\Phi_T(p_T)_d}
\]
is well defined.

Finally, every enumerated bounded finite SCM with an actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\) has some topological order and embeds in the corresponding saturated superarchitecture by the first step.  Its deterministic table system is among the systems counted by \(R_{\max}\), its product source masses define \(p_T\), and \(\rho=\sum_vc_v\).  Selected-law fit and the two margins put \((p_T,\rho)\) in \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\); the essential-feature lemma selects its exact graph branch.  The two inclusions prove equality of the two bounded finite images.  None of these steps proves the legal lifting asked for in \(\text{oeq:universal-legal-lifting}\).

Fix one saturated order and one deterministic response-table system.  Let its \(H\le H_{\max}\) formal source-mass vectors be \(p_1,\ldots,p_H\).  For every coordinate \(y\) of the moment map there are rational table coefficients \(a_y(u_1,\ldots,u_H)\) for which
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_y
 =\sum_{u_1,\ldots,u_H}
   a_y(u_1,\ldots,u_H)\prod_{k=1}^H p_k(u_k).
\]
For a selected cell or \(d\), each coefficient is zero or one; for \(n\), it is either zero or a value of the rational map \(h\).  Thus every moment coordinate is a rational polynomial of degree at most \(H\).  By \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\), a directed-feature polynomial integrates a zero-one table indicator over one copy of every source and has degree at most \(H\).  A source-feature polynomial uses two values of its own source and one value of every other source, so its degree is at most \(H+1\).  Simplex normalization and nonnegativity, the equations
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v)\quad(v\in\Omega_V),
\]
the inequalities \(\delta\le\rho\le1\) and \(\Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta\), the active-incidence conditions in \(\Psi_{T,G}\), and
\[
 \Phi_T(p_T)_n-t\Phi_T(p_T)_d=0
\]
are consequently a finite Boolean combination of rational polynomial sign conditions.  The declared rationality of \(q\), \(\delta\), and \(h\) permits clearing positive common denominators without changing any sign.  By definition, \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\), \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}\), and \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\) bound, respectively, the number, degree, and expanded integer coefficient length of these polynomials.

The saturated architecture definition gives at most \(A_{\max}=N!\) orders.  For a fixed order, every retained equation has all forward directed arguments and every potentially incident source argument, so enumerating the dense tables is exactly the enumeration bounded by \(R_{\max}\).  Missing arrows and sources are not separate architectures: they are encoded by inessential inputs, simplex-vertex ignored sources, and the zero signs prescribed in the graph-legality stratum.  The permitted projected graphs can be represented by a finite disjunction of sign patterns within the same table branch.  Thus there are at most \(A_{\max}R_{\max}\) table branches.

For each branch, all response parameters, including \(\rho\), form one existential block of size at most \(p_{\mathrm{dim}}\), while \(t\) is one free variable.  Apply \(\text{lem:basu-one-block-elimination}\) with \(\omega=1\), \(k_1=p_{\mathrm{dim}}\), and \(\ell=1\).  It returns an equivalent quantifier-free formula in \(t\).  Its ring-operation cost is
\[
 s_{\mathrm{count}}^{\,2(p_{\mathrm{dim}}+1)}
 D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})},
\]
the output degree is \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\), and integer intermediate and output bit lengths are bounded by
\[
 \tau_{\mathrm{eff}}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}.
\]
Multiplication by the number of table branches gives the displayed bound.  Standard exact integer and algebraic-number arithmetic at these bit lengths yields the coarser bit-operation expression
\[
 A_{\max}R_{\max}
 (s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}
 \operatorname{poly}(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}).
\]
Theorem 2.18 of the cited survey is a bound on connected components, not a quantifier-elimination theorem, and is not used here.

The strict feature inequalities remain strict in this formula, so its existential projection is the exact bounded branch of \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\), not the closure of that branch.  If no projected branch is nonempty, the procedure reports INFEASIBLE.  Otherwise every feasible endpoint variable is bounded.  Indeed, pointwise
\[
 h_-\,\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}
 \le h(A^b)\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}
 \le h_+\,\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\},
\]
and expectation gives \(h_-d\le n\le h_+d\).  The intervention margin gives \(d\ge\delta>0\); therefore
\[
 h_-\le t=\frac nd\le h_+.
\]
The projected set is a bounded univariate semialgebraic set.  Between two consecutive real roots of its finitely many output polynomials every sign is constant.  Its infimum and supremum must therefore be either \(h_-\), \(h_+\), or a real root of an output polynomial.  Hence they are real algebraic, have degree \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\), and can be isolated by a Thom encoding.

Fix either isolated endpoint \(t_0\), and regard its Thom encoding as specifying the ordered real algebraic coefficient extension obtained after substitution.  Apply \(\text{lem:basu-sign-sampling}\) to the branch polynomials.  Specializing its algebraic-set polynomial to the zero polynomial makes the ambient zero set the full \(p_{\mathrm{dim}}\)-dimensional response space.  It produces a finite set of real-univariate sample points meeting every semialgebraically connected component of every realizable sign condition; asking also for all signs costs
\[
 s_{\mathrm{count}}^{\,p_{\mathrm{dim}}+1}
 D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}
\]
ring operations, which is dominated by the preceding one-block elimination bound.

If some sample sign vector satisfies all simplex, moment, margin, endpoint, and graph-sign clauses, its real-univariate representation and Thom encoding give algebraic \(p_T,\rho\).  By \(\text{lem:essential-feature-iff}\), the signs in \(\Psi_{T,G}\) verify \(G_S(M_{T,p_T})=G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\), so this is the asserted positive certificate.

Conversely, suppose no sample sign vector satisfies a given branch.  If a response point satisfied it, that point would lie in a semialgebraically connected component of a realizable sign condition of the branch polynomials.  The sample set meets that component, and the defining Boolean formula depends only on the sign vector; its sample would therefore satisfy the same branch, a contradiction.  Hence the branch is empty.  Collecting these sample representations and sign lists for all finitely many branches proves \(\neg\mathsf{Lift}(t_0)\).  A full sign-invariant cylindrical decomposition can be retained instead, but its doubly exponential construction is not the intrinsic complexity asserted here.  Finally, every branch quantified in this argument belongs to the bounded finite compiler.  Thus a negative certificate excludes all and only those enumerated branches; without an affirmative resolution of \(\text{oeq:universal-legal-lifting}\), it does not exclude an equal-moment model in the arbitrary-SCM superclass.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(Q\in R[X_1,\ldots,X_{p_{\mathrm{dim}}}]\) and let \(\mathscr P\) contain at most \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\) polynomials in the same variables, all of degree at most \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}\), over a real closed field \(R\), and let the real dimension of \(\operatorname{Zer}(Q,R^{p_{\mathrm{dim}}})\) be \(p_0\).  There is an algorithm computing a finite set meeting every semialgebraically connected component of every realizable sign condition of \(\mathscr P\) over that zero set in \(s_{\mathrm{count}}^{p_0}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\) ring operations; returning the signs of every polynomial at every sample costs \(s_{\mathrm{count}}^{p_0+1}D_{\mathrm{deg}}^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}\).  The algebraic samples may be recorded by real-univariate representations whose selected roots are specified by Thom encodings.  In particular, taking \(Q=0\) and \(p_0=p_{\mathrm{dim}}\) gives the ambient-space sampling bounds used here.

proposed.name: Saturated ordered response-superarchitecture list
proposed.construction: For each topological order on \(W\), form one saturated superarchitecture containing every forward directed slot and one formal independent source \(U_C\) for every nonempty \(C\subseteq W\).  Thus at most \(A_{\max}=N!\) labeled superarchitectures are generated.  A missing directed arrow is encoded by tables that are constant in that input.  An absent source is encoded by a simplex vertex, with one slot of mass one and the remaining slots of mass zero, and every incident table ignores that source; an all-zero mass vector is never used.  If a formally named \(U_C\) is active only on \(D\subsetneq C\), its realized child set is \(D\).  Before projection, discard empty realized child sets and merge formal sources with the same nonempty realized child set into one tuple source.  For each saturated order enumerate all dense deterministic tables, bounded by \(R_{\max}\), using at most \(K_{\max}=m+3\) slots per formal source, and retain the exact projected selected MAGs \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Use one saturated superarchitecture per order and encode missing structure by inessential inputs and ignored simplex-vertex sources.

proposed.name: Normalized exact graph-legality stratum
proposed.construction:
For a saturated order \(T\), fixed deterministic tables, and masses \(p_T\), retain all directed signs \(Z_{\operatorname{dir}(i,j)}(T,p_T)\) and all formal source-incidence signs \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}(T,p_T)\).  A directed slot is actual exactly when its sign is positive.  For each formal \(U_C\), define its realized child set
\[
D_C(p_T)=\{j\in C:Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}(T,p_T)>0\}.
\]
If \(D_C(p_T)=\varnothing\), normalize the source to a simplex vertex and require every incident table to ignore it.  Discard these absent sources.  Merge all remaining formal sources having the same realized child set \(D_C(p_T)\) into one tuple source indexed canonically by that nonempty set.  Apply the finite latent-and-selection projection rules to the resulting actual directed edges and normalized sources.  The formula \(\Psi_{T,G}(p_T)\) is the Boolean combination of positive and zero incidence signs, the absent-source normalization constraints, and the finite projection test that is true exactly when this projected graph is \(G\).  Every endogenous table comparison in \(Z_e\) ranges over all table inputs, including off-support endogenous assignments.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Interpret exact graph legality from active incidence signs after normalizing formal sources to their realized child sets.

proposed.name: Certified bounded finite legality procedure
proposed.construction: Generate the at most \(A_{\max}=N!\) saturated ordered superarchitectures, enumerate their dense deterministic response-table systems up to \(R_{\max}\), and expand every coordinate of \(\Phi_T\) and every \(Z_e\) coefficient by coefficient as a rational polynomial.  Introduce \(t\) through \(\Phi_T(p_T)_n-t\Phi_T(p_T)_d=0\), and form \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) as the finite disjunction over table systems and \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).  Use one-block existential quantifier elimination to report INFEASIBLE or to produce a univariate sign formula and isolate the algebraic infimum and supremum of the bounded finite image.  At an isolated closure endpoint, decide \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) by sign sampling.  The certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) is either a real-univariate representation with Thom encoding of a satisfying legal response point, or, for every bounded table branch, a finite set of real-univariate sample points with complete sign lists meeting every semialgebraically connected component of every realizable sign condition and proving the branch empty.  A sign-invariant cylindrical decomposition may instead be retained as an optional certificate format, but it is not used for the intrinsic complexity bound.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Replace intrinsic CAD complexity by one-block existential elimination and component-wise sign-sampling certificates.

proposed.statement: For each of at most \(A_{\max}=N!\) topological orders, one saturated superarchitecture containing every forward directed slot and one potential source \(U_C\) for every nonempty \(C\subseteq W\) contains every formerly enumerated architecture: unused directed inputs are inessential, and an absent source is represented by a simplex vertex and ignored by all incident tables.  Sources with the same realized nonempty child set can be merged without changing any structural solution, so at most \(H_{\max}=2^N-1\) active independent sources are needed.  On any fixed permitted architecture, sourcewise barycentric reduction preserves \(\zeta(M)\) with at most \(K_{\max}=m+3\) values per source, after which the model embeds in its saturated ordered superarchitecture and its dense deterministic tables are covered by \(R_{\max}\).  Every point of \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) induces an SCM in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\), and the image of \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) is exactly the intervention-value set of the enumerated bounded finite SCMs satisfying actual selected-MAG legality.  Sourcewise barycentric reduction is asserted to preserve moments, not strict legality; no assertion identifies the bounded image with the image of all arbitrary admissible SCMs.
proposed.justification: This theorem supplies a sound bounded finite candidate language using at most one saturated architecture per topological order, while isolating legal lifting as a separate open problem.
proposed.gap: Source merging and sourcewise cardinality reduction preserve structural solutions or selected moments, but they do not by themselves preserve strict functional-essentiality witnesses under support deletion.
proposed.consumer: It supplies the finite graph-legal candidate language for auditing selection-sensitive intervention bounds in the FCI and LV-IDA workflow of Lee et al.

proposed.justification: The procedure returns exact algebraic endpoint decisions for the bounded finite image with singly exponential one-block complexity.

proposed.consumer: A clinical audit can retain either an algebraic endpoint mechanism or a sample-sign certificate excluding every bounded compiler branch, without misreporting that certificate as a result about arbitrary SCMs.

proposed.comparator_claim: Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 use finite disturbance-response models and polynomial optimization for a fixed canonical DAG; the graph-permitted NPSEM class does not require every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.

The PAG-compatible optimization concerns faithful no-selection SCMs; its edge semantics are generally incomparable with exact actual-parent semantics under positive but potentially unfaithful selection.
Theorem 4.13 identifies marginal DAG models with the same latent projection and Proposition 7.3 commutes intervention with projection, without proving closure of an exact actual-parent stratum.
Proposition 2 gives sourcewise finite-cardinality reduction preserving observed network behavior, not strict essential-source incidences.

Selected-marginalized directed graphs characterize normalized selected interventional indistinguishability, without retaining the absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities calibrated here.

Theorem 4.15 supplies a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm and calculus on specified model classes; the paper distinguishes \(\mathcal M(G)\) from the positive discrete class \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\), whose positivity conditions are not implied by positivity of the selected observed law \(q\).
Theorem 5 gives nonemptiness, openness, and density of faithful distributions in its total-variation Markov model, not an equal-moment legal lift on an unfaithful exact-graph boundary.
Criterion inversion yields consistent set estimators, rates, and confidence regions for identified sets defined by population minimizers.
Width-adaptive endpoint intervals attain uniform asymptotic coverage for an interval-identified scalar as identification width approaches zero.
Resampling and screening followed by a union of graph-specific intervals gives asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal effect after causal discovery.

open_obligations.what_is_open: For a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law \(q\), prove or refute that every arbitrary admissible moment vector and every limit of bounded exact-graph moment vectors has an equal-moment representative in the bounded fiber with actual selected MAG in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The selected-cell and intervention moments are linear in each source law separately, but \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}\) is quadratic in its own source law.  An \(m+3\)-point barycentric reduction can therefore send a positive essentiality witness to zero.  Exact barycenter preservation with prescribed positive witness atoms can fail on a proper face, and the frozen assumptions impose neither faithfulness nor minimum feature strength.  Exogenizing hidden endogenous variables must also preserve actual functional dependencies, not only a permitted latent projection.
open_obligations.attempted: Directed-feature indicators can be appended to the sourcewise moment vector because they are separately linear, but the two-copy source-feature polynomial remains nonlinear in the compressed source.  Retaining an explicit witness pair does not guarantee exact barycenter preservation with positive weights.  The positive exclusive-or support-deletion family demonstrates failure of the naive route, although its illegal boundary has an equal-moment legal lift and is not a negative certificate.  The compelled-collider case closes only for an isolated selection root, as recorded in the partial result.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The mandatory collider test closes for the following nontrivial subcase.  Let \(V=\{X,Y,Z\}\) be binary, let the retained structural graph be \(X\to Z\leftarrow Y\), let \(S\) be an independent selection root, take \(B=\{X\}\), and assume the positive selected law \(q\) obeys \(X\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}Y\).  Put
\[
p_{xy}=q(Z=1\mid X=x,Y=y)\in(0,1).
\]
Choose independent \(U_X,U_Y\) with laws \(q_X,q_Y\), an independent \(U_Z\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and measurable sets \(E_{xy}\subset[0,1]\) of Lebesgue measure \(p_{xy}\).  The four sets can be chosen so that \(E_{0y}\ne E_{1y}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(y\), and \(E_{x0}\ne E_{x1}\) modulo null sets for at least one \(x\): start with intervals of the prescribed lengths and, whenever an equality remains, exchange two sufficiently short subintervals between the set and its complement.  Since \(0<p_{xy}<1\), each exchange is possible; finitely many disjoint exchanges preserve distinctions already installed.  Define
\[
X=U_X,\qquad Y=U_Y,\qquad Z=\mathbf 1\{U_Z\in E_{XY}\}.
\]
Then
\[
\Pr(X=x,Y=y,Z=z)=q_X(x)q_Y(y)q(z\mid x,y)=q(x,y,z),
\]
and the strict symmetric differences make both arrows into \(Z\) actual functional dependencies, even when \(q\) is unfaithful to one or both arrows.  Taking an independent \(S\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\rho)\), with \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\), gives \(c_v=\rho q(v)\) and \(d=\rho\).  For every bounded binary outcome map \(h\), recursive truncated factorization gives the single selected-intervention value
\[
\theta=
\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}}q_Y(y)
\bigl[h(0)(1-p_{by})+h(1)p_{by}\bigr].
\]
It is attained by the exact collider construction.  Hence the exact-graph value and every response-support boundary representation of it have a legal lift in this isolated-selection compelled-collider case.  This does not cover selected MAGs in which \(S\) has parents or latent ancestors, and it does not preserve an arbitrary pair \((n,d)\) beyond the value fixed by this collider factorization.

prose_updates.tldr: This note studies bounded finite graph-legal response fibers for selection COPAGs without claiming that the full positive, potentially unfaithful arbitrary-SCM fiber is closed.  One saturated superarchitecture per topological order gives at most \(N!\) architecture branches before dense table enumeration; exact essential-feature signs determine the actual selected MAG, and singly exponential one-block real-algebraic procedures return algebraic endpoint witnesses or certificates excluding all bounded compiler branches.  Universal legal lifting and full-fiber closure remain open.  Independently, the graph-free selected-law and two-margin premises imply an explicit finite-state envelope whose endpoints are attained in the complete all-circle one-source subclass and therefore in every permitted family containing those witnesses.  The binary interval \([1/20,39/40]\) is an audit instance, and confidence-fiber inference provides finite-sample outer coverage for the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery use case of Lee et al.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm on specified model classes; Yang et al. optimize over faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; Duarte et al. optimize a fixed canonical DAG; and Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models. None settles whether the exact actual-parent COPAG fiber for a positive, potentially unfaithful selected law is closed or has attained endpoints. This note also leaves that general question open, while formalizing it and proving bounded-finite and saturated special-case results.
project_justification.niche: The tractable object constructed here is the bounded finite graph-legal response fiber, a finite union of semialgebraic strata. Its essential-feature signs determine the exact selected MAG, and real-algebraic procedures decide whether a boundary value of this bounded image has a legal representative or is excluded from all bounded branches. Equality with, and closure or attainment of, the full arbitrary-SCM fiber remain exactly oeq:universal-legal-lifting.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an invariant essential-feature index and exact polynomial legality test, one saturated superarchitecture for each topological order, and singly exponential existential-semialgebraic endpoint certificates for the bounded finite image.  It proves a graph-free finite-state outer envelope, one-source endpoint attainment for the complete all-circle COPAG, and the resulting sandwich transfer to every permitted family containing those witnesses.  It designates the compelled-collider case as the first unresolved kill test for universal legal lifting and retains finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage without asserting endpoint convergence for the full arbitrary-SCM fiber.

prose_updates.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes define maximal ancestral graphs under latent marginalization and selection conditioning.  Evans canonicalizes latent DAG margins and makes latent projection commute with intervention, but these model-equivalence results do not close an exact functional-essentiality stratum.  Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe give sourcewise cardinality reduction preserving network behavior, not strict source-incidence witnesses.  Duarte et al. fix a canonical DAG and optimize graph-permitted finite-disturbance NPSEMs without requiring every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.  Yang et al. treat faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; that faithful edge semantics is generally incomparable with the actual-parent semantics used here under potentially unfaithful selection.  Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models, which do not retain the absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities calibrated by the two margins.  Chen and Mooij are closest: they give a sound-and-complete identification algorithm and calculus, while distinguishing \(\mathcal M(G)\) from \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\); positivity of the selected observed law \(q\) is not equated here with every positivity condition defining their positive discrete class.  Boeken, Forré, and Mooij establish openness and density of faithful laws, which does not produce an equal-moment lift on an unfaithful boundary.  Basu supplies the critical-point sign-sampling and one-block quantifier-elimination results used for the bounded compiler's certificates and complexity.  Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer, Imbens and Manski, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky inform confidence-set inversion; the formal inference claim here remains finite-sample outer coverage.  Lee et al. are the clinical consumer: their FCI and LV-IDA analysis conditions on discharge alive and acknowledges both selection bias and graph ambiguity.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: A positive exclusive-or support-deletion family can hold the selected law and intervention moments fixed while an actual shared-source incidence vanishes, so ordinary moment compression does not preserve exact graph legality.  Saturated superarchitectures remove redundant subset enumeration but do not repair this topological obstruction.  A negative algebraic certificate excludes every bounded finite compiler branch at the tested value; absent universal legal lifting, it cannot exclude an equal-moment repair in the arbitrary-SCM superclass.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved scope comprises source merging by realized child set, sourcewise moment preservation on a fixed permitted architecture, saturated ordered superarchitecture embedding, exact polynomial legality for bounded finite response models, singly exponential one-block endpoint decisions for the bounded image, the transferable saturated envelope, and finite-sample confidence-set event inclusion.  Equality between arbitrary selected SCMs and the bounded compiler, preservation of exact graph legality under general source compression, and closure or attainment of the full positive unfaithful fiber remain open.  No faithfulness, density, minimum edge strength, or positivity of every essential-feature polynomial is added.  In particular, positivity of selected \(q\) is not treated as the stronger positivity defining another paper's model class, and a bounded-branch non-lift is not a superclass impossibility result.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem supplies a sound bounded finite response language using at most one saturated architecture per topological order while isolating legal lifting as a separate open problem.
statement_notes.gap: Merging and sourcewise cardinality reduction preserve structural solutions or moments but do not by themselves preserve strict actual-parent and shared-source witnesses.
statement_notes.consumer: It gives the finite candidate language for auditing selection-sensitive bounds in the FCI and LV-IDA workflow of Lee et al.

statement_notes.justification: The procedure returns exact algebraic endpoint decisions for the bounded finite image with singly exponential one-block complexity.
statement_notes.gap: Existing fixed-graph programs do not certify exact selected-MAG sign strata across COPAG-compatible bounded branches.
statement_notes.consumer: The clinical audit can retain an algebraic endpoint mechanism or a sign-sample certificate excluding all bounded branches, with no claim about the arbitrary-SCM superclass.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the sole nonroutine topological bottleneck between exact actual-parent graph semantics and attained extrema for the full arbitrary-SCM class.
statement_notes.gap: Openness and density of faithful laws do not supply an equal-moment lift on an unfaithful boundary or an unattained causal endpoint.
statement_notes.consumer: Its resolution determines whether exact-graph COPAG bounds beyond the bounded compiler and saturated subclass may be reported as attained without extra graph-strength assumptions.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be the complete all-circle COPAG.  If \(M\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\), the definition of the admissible class supplies \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\) such that
\[
c_v(M)=\rho q(v)\quad(v\in\Omega_V),
\qquad d_M\geq\delta.
\]
The graph-free part of Theorem \(\text{
m thm:saturated-envelope-transfer}\) therefore gives
\[
L_\delta\leq\theta(M)\leq U_\delta.
\]
Taking the image over all members of the admissible class proves
\[
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\subseteq[L_\delta,U_\delta].
\]

We next verify that the witness family from that theorem satisfies the exact graph stratum.  For every \(t\in[0,1]\), its unique exogenous source, or the deterministic latent-root copy of that source, is an actual essential parent of every \(X\in V\).  This uses the hypothesis that every observed state space has at least two elements and the positive-selected-law assumption \(q(v)>0\) for every joint cell.  Hence, for any distinct \(X,Y\in V\), the minimal structural graph contains the latent fork
\[
X\leftarrow L\rightarrow Y.
\]
Its internal vertex is latent and is a noncollider, so the definition of latent projection makes \(X\) and \(Y\) adjacent.  Retaining and then selecting on \(S\) does not delete this inducing adjacency.  Thus the selected MAG \(G_S(M_t)\) has complete skeleton on \(V\).

A complete mixed graph has no nonadjacent pair.  Therefore no pair can be separated, since its length-one edge is an open path under every conditioning set disjoint from the endpoints.  Thus every complete selected MAG has the empty nontrivial separation model.  Equivalently, it lies in the Markov-equivalence class represented by the complete all-circle COPAG: there are no unshielded triples or discriminating paths with nonadjacent endpoints that could force an invariant endpoint mark.  Consequently,
\[
G_S(M_t)\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P).
\]
The remaining properties of the constructed family are
\[
c_v(M_t)=\delta q(v),\qquad \rho=\delta\in[\delta,1],\qquad d_{M_t}=1\geq\delta.
\]
Hence \(M_t\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) for every \(t\).  Applying the transfer clause of Theorem \(\text{
m thm:saturated-envelope-transfer}\) with \(\mathcal C=\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) proves
\[
\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=[L_\delta,U_\delta].
\]
At \(t=0\) and \(t=1\), the construction has one source and at most \(m+1\) positive-mass response types, proving endpoint attainment with the claimed cardinality.

If \(h\) is constant, then \(h_-=h_+\) and every summand involving \(h(A(v))-h_-\) or \(h_+-h(A(v))\) vanishes.  The envelope definition gives
\[
L_\delta=U_\delta=h_-,
\]
so the equality already proved reduces to \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=\{h_-\}\).

For completeness, consider the separately stated vacuous-intervention boundary case, in which \(B=\varnothing\) and the hard-intervention submodel is the factual model.  For every admissible \(M\), recursive consistency and the selected-law-fit assumption give
\[
d_M=\Pr_M(S=1)=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}c_v(M)=\rho\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}q(v)=\rho
\]
and
\[
n_M=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}h(A(v))c_v(M)
=\rho\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}q(v)h(A(v)).
\]
The population margin gives \(\rho\geq\delta>0\), so division is valid and
\[
\theta(M)=\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}q(v)h(A(v)).
\]
To show that the exact-graph fiber is nonempty, take one source with states \(u_v\) of masses \(\delta q(v)\), and, when \(\delta<1\), one additional state \(u_0\) of mass \(1-\delta\).  Put \(V(u_v)=v\) and \(S(u_v)=1\), while \(S(u_0)=0\) and \(V(u_0)\) is arbitrary.  Then \(c_v=\delta q(v)\), \(\rho=d_M=\delta\), and all margin conditions hold.  Positivity of \(q\) and the assumption of at least two states per observed variable make the common source essential for every observed vertex.  The preceding latent-fork argument therefore puts its selected MAG in the complete all-circle class.  This admissible witness proves that the vacuous-intervention fiber is exactly the asserted singleton.

added_lemmas.statement:
Suppose \(|\Omega_B|\geq 2\).  Every recursive SCM \(M\) for which there exists \(\rho\in[\delta,1]\) satisfying \(c_v(M)=\rho q(v)\) for all \(v\in\Omega_V\) and \(d_M\geq\delta\) obeys
\[
L_\delta\leq\theta(M)\leq U_\delta.
\]
This conclusion is graph-free.  Moreover, there is a family \((M_t:t\in[0,1])\) of one-source recursive SCMs satisfying \(c_v(M_t)=\delta q(v)\) for every \(v\), \(d_{M_t}=1\), and
\[
\theta(M_t)=(1-t)L_\delta+tU_\delta.
\]
If every observed state space has at least two elements and \(q(v)>0\) for every \(v\), the family can be chosen so that the unique source, or its deterministic latent-root copy, is an actual essential parent of every vertex in \(V\).  Each endpoint model has at most \(m+1\) positive-mass response types.  Consequently, for any family \(\mathcal C\) of recursive SCMs satisfying the displayed graph-free premises and containing every \(M_t\),
\[
\{\theta(M):M\in\mathcal C\}=[L_\delta,U_\delta].
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put
\[
I_b=\{v\in\Omega_V:B(v)=b\},\qquad
T_- =\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h(A(v))-h_-\},\qquad
T_+ =\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h_+-h(A(v))\}.
\]
The definition of \(h_-\) and \(h_+\) gives \(T_-\geq0\) and \(T_+\geq0\).  Fix a model satisfying the premises.  The intervention-margin assumption and \(\delta>0\) give
\[
d_M\geq\delta>0,
\]
so \(\theta(M)=n_M/d_M\) is defined.  We first record the consistency step used below.  Fix an exogenous realization for which the factual solution has \(B=b\).  Replacing the structural equations for the coordinates of \(B\) by the constants equal to their already realized values leaves those coordinates unchanged.  Induction along a topological order of the recursive SCM then leaves every later endogenous coordinate unchanged.  Thus, on every factual event \(\{V=v,S=1\}\) with \(v\in I_b\),
\[
A^b=A(v),\qquad S^b=1.
\]
This is the recursive-SCM consistency identity, derived here from recursiveness and the definition of a hard intervention.

The events \(\{V=v,S=1\}\), \(v\in I_b\), are disjoint.  Since \(h(A^b)-h_-\geq0\), consistency, the selected-law-fit assumption, and the population-margin assumption imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
n_M-h_-d_M
&=\mathbb E_M\!\left[(h(A^b)-h_-)\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}\right]\\
&\geq \sum_{v\in I_b}\{h(A(v))-h_-\}\Pr_M(V=v,S=1)\\
&=\rho T_-\\
&\geq\delta T_-.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because a probability satisfies \(d_M\leq1\), division by the positive \(d_M\) yields
\[
\theta(M)-h_-
=\frac{n_M-h_-d_M}{d_M}
\geq\frac{\delta T_-}{d_M}
\geq\delta T_-.
\]
By the definition of the saturated envelope, the last inequality is \(\theta(M)\geq L_\delta\).  Applying the same argument to the nonnegative map \(h_+-h\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_+d_M-n_M
&=\mathbb E_M\!\left[(h_+-h(A^b))\mathbf 1\{S^b=1\}\right]\\
&\geq \sum_{v\in I_b}\{h_+-h(A(v))\}\Pr_M(V=v,S=1)\\
&=\rho T_+\\
&\geq\delta T_+,
\end{aligned}
\]
and hence
\[
h_+-\theta(M)\geq\delta T_+,
\qquad
\theta(M)\leq U_\delta.
\]
No graph property was used in these two inequalities.

We now construct the asserted family.  Finiteness of \(\Omega_A\) supplies states \(a_-\) and \(a_+\) such that \(h(a_-)=h_-\) and \(h(a_+)=h_+\).  Since \(|\Omega_B|\geq2\), choose \(b^\dagger\in\Omega_B\setminus\{b\}\).  For \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\), write
\[
\lambda_-(t)=1-t,\qquad \lambda_+(t)=t.
\]
Give one exogenous variable \(U\) a state \(u_{v,\sigma}\) of mass
\[
\Pr(U=u_{v,\sigma})=\lambda_\sigma(t)\delta q(v)
\]
whenever this mass is positive.  If \(\delta<1\), also give it a state \(u_{0,\sigma}\) of mass \(\lambda_\sigma(t)(1-\delta)\) whenever that mass is positive.  Zero-mass states are omitted.  Since \(q\) is a probability mass function,
\[
\sum_{\sigma}\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}\lambda_\sigma(t)\delta q(v)
+\sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma(t)(1-\delta)
=\delta+(1-\delta)=1.
\]

Use a recursive order with the coordinates of \(B\) first, followed by those of \(V\setminus B\), and then \(S\).  On \(u_{v,\sigma}\), set the factual value of \(B\) equal to \(B(v)\), and prescribe the tables for \(V\setminus B\) at input \(B(v)\) so that the factual retained vector is \(v\).  At input \(B=b\), keep \(A=A(v)\) when \(B(v)=b\), and set \(A=a_\sigma\) when \(B(v)\neq b\).  On \(u_{0,\sigma}\), set the factual value of \(B\) to \(b^\dagger\), choose arbitrary factual values for \(V\setminus B\), and set \(A=a_\sigma\) at input \(B=b\).  There is no conflict: an entry prescribed both factually and interventionally has \(B(v)=b\), where both prescriptions use \(A(v)\), while \(b^\dagger\neq b\).  Complete every unmentioned table entry arbitrarily.

For selection, prescribe
\[
S(B(v),u_{v,\sigma})=1,
\qquad
S(b,u_{v,\sigma})=1,
\]
and, for a remainder state,
\[
S(b^\dagger,u_{0,\sigma})=0,
\qquad
S(b,u_{0,\sigma})=1.
\]
The two prescriptions in the first display agree when \(B(v)=b\), and those in the second display concern distinct inputs.  Thus they define compatible deterministic response tables and hence a recursive SCM \(M_t\).

Factually, exactly the states \(u_{v,\sigma}\) are selected.  Therefore, for every \(v\),
\[
c_v(M_t)=\sum_\sigma\lambda_\sigma(t)\delta q(v)=\delta q(v),
\qquad \rho=\delta\in[\delta,1].
\]
Under \(do(B=b)\), every positive-mass source state is selected, so
\[
d_{M_t}=1\geq\delta.
\]
Let
\[
E_-=\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)h(A(v))
+\left(1-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\right)h_-,
\]
and define \(E_+\) by replacing \(h_-\) in the second term by \(h_+\).  The intervention table just constructed gives
\[
n_{M_t}=(1-t)E_-+tE_+.
\]
Direct expansion of the saturated-envelope definition gives
\[
E_-=h_-+\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h(A(v))-h_-\}=L_\delta
\]
and
\[
E_+=h_+-\delta\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\{h_+-h(A(v))\}=U_\delta.
\]
Since \(d_{M_t}=1\), it follows that
\[
\theta(M_t)=(1-t)L_\delta+tU_\delta.
\]
Also, with \(Q_b=\sum_{v\in I_b}q(v)\),
\[
U_\delta-L_\delta=(h_+-h_-)(1-\delta Q_b)\geq0,
\]
because \(0\leq Q_b\leq1\) and \(0<\delta\leq1\).  Hence these values range over the entire closed interval.

At \(t=0\) or \(t=1\), only one sign of the source states remains.  Strict positivity of \(q\) makes all \(m\) states \(u_{v,\sigma}\) positive, and there is at most one additional remainder state, so an endpoint uses at most \(m+1\) positive-mass response types.

It remains to establish the asserted essential-parent property.  Fix a sign \(\sigma\) with \(\lambda_\sigma(t)>0\).  If \(X\in B\), choose two joint cells \(v,v'\) that differ in their \(X\)-coordinate.  If \(X\in V\setminus B\), fix any \(\beta\in\Omega_B\) and choose two cells \(v,v'\) with \(B(v)=B(v')=\beta\) but different \(X\)-coordinates.  Such cells exist because the state space of \(X\) has at least two elements.  Positivity of \(q\), together with \(\delta>0\) and \(\lambda_\sigma(t)>0\), makes both corresponding source states positive.  The factual table prescriptions give different outputs for \(X\) at these two source states, with every endogenous input to the \(X\)-table held fixed in the second case.  Thus the source is functionally essential for every \(X\in V\) outside exogenous null sets.  If the graph formalism represents only endogenous vertices, insert the deterministic latent root \(L=U\) and use \(L\) as the common input; this changes neither the retained law nor the number of positive-mass response types.

Finally, let \(\mathcal C\) satisfy the last assertion.  The graph-free inequalities give
\[
\{\theta(M):M\in\mathcal C\}\subseteq[L_\delta,U_\delta],
\]
whereas containment of every \(M_t\) and the displayed affine formula give the reverse inclusion.  This proves equality and the transfer claim.

proposed.statement: If \(\mathcal P\) is the complete all-circle COPAG, every observed variable has at least two states, and \(|\Omega_B|\ge2\), then \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=[L_\delta,U_\delta]\), where \(L_\delta\) and \(U_\delta\) are given by the closed-form saturated envelope. Both endpoints are attained by a one-source SCM with at most \(m+1\) positive-mass response types. If \(h\) is constant, the interval is the singleton \(\{h_-\}\); if the intervention is vacuous, the fiber is the singleton \(\{\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}q(v)h(A(v))\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the graph-free universal envelope and sandwich-transfer result into the declared proof spine while preserving the exact complete-COPAG claim.
